Climate Blame Game: Global Central Planning Needed?

9 hours ago
Guest Blogger
6 Comments

By Robert Bradley Jr.

Listen to audio version of this article
Sponsored by
0:00 / 2:36
Instaread

“Buyer beware. The smartest guys in the room, the expert planners, the government-enabled Lords of the (political) marketplace, want to demote you.”

Central holistic planning (think global government) is needed to organize a dysfunctional world. That is what the climate architects dream about. Enter “planet regeneration” and “macro-systemic architect” Greg Reynolds, who has the post below on social media. It concerns one utility practice; there are thousands more needed to “save” the planet. From the center.

This post from Behavior x Climate names something I’ve watched for years: the climate blame game. Consumers point at corporations. Corporations point to demand. Governments point at voters. Around and around. Progress slows. The planet burns.

Continuing:

But here’s what the post doesn’t name—because it’s the part we’ve all been trained not to see: Every player in that loop is already spending money that could be healing. The utility spends billions on grid upgrades that don’t fix watersheds. The data center spends millions on water compliance that doesn’t restore rivers. The ratepayer spends hours in time poverty and dollars in debt service—none of it visible as a contribution.

This isn’t a failure of intention. It’s a failure of sight. When a utility can’t see the watershed that cools its generators, it spends on compliance instead of restoration. When a data center can’t see the community that hosts it, it spends on permits instead of partnership. When a ratepayer can’t see their own … fragmented value, they carry debt instead of receiving dividends. The blame game persists because no one can see the whole.

“…the whole.” But God-in-the-machine ‘regenerationist’ Reynolds has a master plan.

But here’s what becomes possible when sight is restored:

The utility’s grid upgrades become watershed restoration. The data center’s compliance dollars become community dividends. The ratepayer’s fragmented value becomes financial resilience. Not new money. Better use of money already moving.

Not blame. Visibility. Not “who’s responsible?” but “who’s ready to see the whole?”

The question the post asks is the right one. The answer isn’t more finger-pointing. It’s a lens that finally lets every player see what they’ve been missing—and act on it. Watch the Video: Truth starts at Point Zero. The hive does the rest.

Buyer beware. The smartest guys in the room; the expert planners; the government-enabled Lords of the (political) marketplace want to demote you. Your plans, made with your resources, are to be subject to that one institution with a monopoly on the initiation of force: government.

Buyers and sellers, billions of us, subjecting their will to the ‘Common Good’? Just say No.
